content: I finally gave this site the redesign it has needed for a while. For years it was a fairly generic theme — clean, but it could have been anyone’s. That never sat right with me, because the things I actually spend my time on are not generic at all. I write software during the day, I solder and 3D-print strange contraptions on the weekend, and somewhere in between I paint and sketch. I wanted a home on the internet that holds all of that in one place. So the new site leans into three threads: Software — the apps, tools, and libraries I build, including the ones I’m shipping through Vaazh Studios. Hardware — the weekend builds, prints, and prototypes. Art — the slower, quieter practice that keeps me patient. Why start writing? Building things teaches you a lot, but the lessons evaporate if you never write them down. This blog is where I’ll keep the notes: what I tried, what broke, what I’d do differently. Some posts will be technical, some will be about a print that failed six times before it worked, and some will just be me thinking out loud. If any of that is interesting to you, stick around. More soon.

content: A short note on what’s currently on my bench, mostly so future-me remembers what this month felt like. Pose Studio The big one is Pose Studio, a camera app for iOS and Android that gives real-time pose guidance from a quick draft photo. It’s the first app I’m shipping under Vaazh Studios, and there’s a waitlist open while I get it ready. On the workshop side The 3D printer has barely cooled down lately. Most of it is functional prints — brackets, jigs, repairs — but a few playful builds have snuck in too. I’ll write those up properly once they actually work. What’s next I want to get into a rhythm of shipping small things often, and writing a little about each one. If that sounds like your kind of thing, the projects page is the best place to follow along.
